title: 不 vs 没有 in Chinese: HSK 1 Grammar with Examples
description: When to use 不 (bù) and when to use 没有 (méiyǒu) in Chinese: habits and plans, the past, "not yet", 有, questions, common mistakes and HSK 1 examples.
h1: 不 vs 没有: Which Negative to Use
lede: Chinese has two everyday ways to say "not". 不 (bù) is for habits, plans, wishes and how things are. 没有 (méiyǒu) is for things that did not happen or have not happened yet, and it is the only way to say "don't have".

paras: Use 不 for what you do or don't do in general, and for what you will or won't do. Use 没有 when an action did not happen in the past, or has not happened so far.
Both go straight before the verb. Compare 我不去学校 (I'm not going to school) with 我没有去学校 (I didn't go to school).

examples.en: I'm not going to school tomorrow.
I didn't go to school yesterday.

sections.h2: 不 with 是, adjectives and "can"
paras: 不 is always used with 是, and normally with adjectives such as 冷 or 忙 and with words like 会, 想, 认识 and 知道. This is true even when you talk about the past: 昨天不冷 means "it wasn't cold yesterday".
不 is normally said bù, but it changes to bú before a fourth-tone syllable: 不是 bú shì, 不去 bú qù, 不会 bú huì.
没有 says that something did not happen. With 还 in front, it means "not yet". In speech, 没有 before a verb is often shortened to 没.

The most common mistake is to use 不 for the past: 我昨天不去学校 is wrong for "I didn't go to school yesterday"; it sounds as if you had decided not to go. Another mistake is to add 了 to the verb after 没有. 没有 already says the action did not happen, so say 我没有吃饭, not 我没有吃饭了.

examples.zh: 我昨天很忙，没有看电视。
examples.py: Wǒ zuótiān hěn máng, méiyǒu kàn diànshì.
examples.en: I was busy yesterday, so I didn't watch TV.

paras: The verb 有 (to have, there is) is never used with 不. "I don't have" is always 我没有, never 我不有, and this is true for the past, present and future.

examples.en: He doesn't have an older brother.

paras: You can ask a question by putting the positive and negative forms side by side. In this pattern 不 is said lightly, with no tone. To ask whether something has happened, put 没有 at the end after 了.
To answer "no", repeat the negative with the verb: 不去 (no, I'm not going), 没有 (no, I didn't / I don't have), or 还没有 (not yet).

examples.py: Nǐ míngtiān qù bu qù xuéxiào?
examples.en: Are you going to school tomorrow?
Do you have a Chinese name?

worksheet.description: A free printable 不 vs 没有 worksheet for HSK 1: 20 exercises (choose the negative, word order, fix the mistake) with an answer key.

exercises.instructions: Write 不 or 没有 in each gap. The English tells you what the sentence means.

items.en: I didn't go to school yesterday.
I'm not going to the shop tomorrow.
He didn't come to class last week.

items.en: Have you seen that film? I haven't seen it yet.

exercises.instructions: Write the words as one correct sentence.

exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Write the correct sentence.
